unit.title: HTTP over TCP: boundaries, failures, and testable design
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student beginning deliberate software-engineering practice
unit.scope: Implement and test a deliberately small HTTP/1.1 response reader over loopback TCP, with explicit framing, limits, timeouts, error taxonomy, and observable behavior.
learning_objectives: Distinguish a TCP byte stream from application-level messages.
Turn a small protocol subset into an explicit, reviewable contract.
Separate transport, parsing, policy, and observability concerns.
Use deterministic tests to exercise fragmentation and failure paths.
Document deliberate limitations without presenting a teaching implementation as production-ready.
required_inputs: A locally available programming language with TCP socket and test support
deliverables: Source code for the bounded client and response reader
Deterministic automated tests using only loopback or in-memory byte streams
A README with run commands and supported/unsupported behavior
A short engineering report with test evidence and reflection
out_of_scope: TLS, DNS, proxies, redirects, caching, cookies, authentication, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3
A general-purpose or production HTTP client
Claims about the upstream lecture order, textbook chapter order, or exam coverage
Completion of the approximately 40-hour catalog course

unit_completion_requires: All declared learner deliverables are present.
A worker-harness-controlled validator executes the relevant automated tests.
The validator confirms that required success and failure cases are evidenced by captured results.
The submission satisfies the independent examiner rubric and its critical gates.
acceptable_evidence: Validator-captured test command, exit status, and logs
Written report and comprehension responses tied to the submitted implementation
insufficient_evidence: A learner or agent prose claim of completion
Files that were not exercised by the controlled validator
Successful processing of only one unfragmented happy-path response
completion_policy.kickoff_effect: Passing this unit may complete only kickoff_01_http_over_tcp.

course_completion.reason: The catalog describes a roughly 40-hour course, while this package defines one approximately 6-hour manager-authored kickoff. Later validated units and an explicit course-level policy are required.
